domain.name: Frontend Engineer
domain.description: From HTML and CSS to modern frameworks, accessibility, and web performance.

skills.name: HTML Fundamentals

skills.name: CSS Fundamentals

skills.name: JavaScript Basics
skills.description: Variables, functions, objects, arrays, and control flow in modern JS.

skills.name: Git and Version Control
skills.description: Track changes, branch, merge, and collaborate with Git.

skills.name: CSS Layout (Flexbox & Grid)

skills.name: DOM Manipulation

skills.name: Async JavaScript

skills.name: Responsive Design

skills.name: HTTP and APIs

skills.name: TypeScript Fundamentals

skills.name: React Fundamentals

skills.name: State Management

skills.name: Forms and Validation

skills.name: Accessibility (a11y)
skills.description: Build inclusive UIs with semantics, keyboard support, and screen readers in mind.

skills.name: Client-Side Routing
skills.description: Navigate between views with a router and handle params, nested routes, and guards.

skills.name: Frontend Testing
skills.description: Write unit and integration tests for components and user flows.

skills.name: CSS Architecture

skills.name: Web Performance

skills.name: Frontend Architecture

questions.prompt: Which HTML tag is best for the primary heading of a page?
questions.explanation: One <h1> per page is best for SEO and screen readers. <head> and <title> are metadata, <header> is a landmark.

questions.prompt: What does the alt attribute on an do?

options.text: Provides fallback text for screen readers and broken images

questions.explanation: alt text is essential for accessibility and displayed if the image fails to load.

questions.prompt: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: Specificity order: inline > #id > .class > element. IDs beat classes; classes beat elements.

questions.prompt: What does the CSS box model consist of (inside to outside)?
questions.explanation: Content → Padding → Border → Margin. box-sizing: border-box includes padding+border in width.

questions.prompt: Which keyword declares a constant in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: const declares a block-scoped binding that can't be reassigned. Use it by default.

questions.prompt: The difference between == and === in JavaScript is:

options.text: == does type coercion; === requires matching types

questions.explanation: === is strict equality — no type coercion. Prefer it to avoid surprising conversions like '1' == 1.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of feature branches in Git?

options.text: Isolate work so main stays stable

questions.explanation: Feature branches keep experimental work off main until it's reviewed and ready.

questions.prompt: Which Flexbox property controls horizontal alignment of items along the main axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content aligns along the main axis (horizontal for row). align-items aligns along the cross axis.

questions.prompt: In CSS Grid, which property defines the columns of a grid container?
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns defines the column track sizes, e.g. repeat(3, 1fr) or 200px 1fr 1fr.

questions.prompt: Which DOM method selects the first element matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector returns the first match. querySelectorAll returns all matches as a NodeList.

questions.prompt: What does event.preventDefault() do in an event handler?

options.text: Prevents the browser's default action (e.g., form submission)

questions.explanation: preventDefault cancels the default behavior. stopPropagation stops bubbling — they're different.

questions.prompt: What does async/await do in JavaScript?

options.text: Allows writing asynchronous code in a synchronous-looking style over promises

questions.explanation: async/await is syntactic sugar over promises — the function still returns a promise.

questions.prompt: In the event loop, which queue runs before setTimeout callbacks?
questions.explanation: Micro-tasks (promise callbacks) run to completion before the next macro-task (setTimeout, I/O).

questions.prompt: What is the mobile-first approach to responsive design?

options.text: Design for desktop first, then shrink
Design for mobile first, then enhance for larger screens with min-width media queries

questions.explanation: Mobile-first starts with the smallest layout and progressively enhances upward with min-width queries.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct fetch call to GET JSON from an API?
questions.explanation: fetch returns a Response; you must call .json() on it to parse the body.

questions.prompt: What is CORS and why does it matter?

options.text: A browser security policy that blocks cross-origin requests unless the server opts in

questions.explanation: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) lets servers control which origins can read their responses.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between TypeScript `interface` and `type`?

options.text: Interfaces can be merged/extended; type aliases can express unions and tuples

questions.explanation: Interfaces are open to declaration merging; types are more expressive for unions, intersections, and tuples.

questions.prompt: In React, what does the dependency array in useEffect control?

options.text: When the effect re-runs — it re-runs when any dependency changes

questions.explanation: Empty array = run once. Missing array = run every render. With deps = run when they change.

questions.prompt: Why does React warn about missing `key` props in lists?

options.text: Keys help React identify which items changed, added, or removed for efficient reconciliation

questions.explanation: Stable keys let React's diffing algorithm avoid re-rendering the whole list.

questions.prompt: What is React Context used for?

options.text: Sharing state across a tree without prop drilling

questions.explanation: Context provides values to descendants without passing props through every intermediate component.

questions.prompt: When would you choose a global store (Redux, Zustand) over local state?

options.text: When many distant components need to read or write the same state

questions.explanation: Local state is simpler. Global stores earn their keep when state is shared across unrelated parts of the tree.

questions.prompt: Why is controlled input important in React forms?

options.text: The input value lives in React state, so it's always in sync for validation and submission

questions.explanation: Controlled inputs store value in state, giving you full control over validation and formatting.

questions.prompt: Which is a good practice for form validation UX?

options.text: Validate on blur, then on change after the first error

questions.explanation: Validating on blur avoids nagging while typing; switching to on-change after the first error gives fast feedback.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum contrast ratio recommended by WCAG AA for body text?
questions.explanation: WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.

questions.prompt: Why should interactive elements be keyboard accessible?

options.text: Users who can't use a mouse rely on Tab, Enter, Space, and arrow keys

questions.explanation: Keyboard access is a foundational a11y requirement. Use semantic elements and manage focus well.

questions.prompt: In React Router, which component triggers navigation without a full page reload?
questions.explanation: <Link> uses client-side navigation — no full page reload — while preserving browser history.

questions.prompt: What does client-side routing primarily improve?

options.text: Perceived speed by avoiding full page reloads

questions.explanation: Client-side routing swaps views without round-tripping to the server for HTML — smooth SPAs. SSR helps SEO separately.

questions.prompt: Which library is most commonly used with React for unit/component testing?
questions.explanation: React Testing Library encourages testing the way users interact. Works well with Vitest or Jest.

questions.prompt: The testing pyramid suggests you should have:

options.text: More unit tests than integration, more integration than E2E

questions.explanation: Unit tests are fast and numerous; E2E is slow and few. Balance keeps the suite fast and reliable.

questions.prompt: What is the primary benefit of CSS variables (custom properties)?

options.text: Centralized design tokens that can be reused and changed at runtime

questions.explanation: CSS variables (--color-primary) let you theme dynamically and keep design tokens consistent.

questions.prompt: Utility-first CSS (like Tailwind) means:

options.text: Composing small single-purpose classes directly in markup

questions.explanation: Utility classes (flex, p-4, text-sm) are combined to build styles without custom CSS per component.

questions.prompt: What does Core Web Vitals measure?

options.text: User-experience metrics like LCP, INP, and CLS

questions.explanation: LCP (load), INP (interactivity), CLS (visual stability) — Google's user experience metrics used for SEO ranking.

questions.prompt: What is code splitting in a bundler?

options.text: Breaking the bundle into smaller chunks loaded on demand

questions.explanation: Dynamic imports (import()) create separate chunks so users only download what they need for the current route.

questions.prompt: What is tree shaking?

options.text: Dead code elimination — bundlers drop unused exports from the bundle

questions.explanation: Tree shaking relies on ESM's static analysis — only imported parts of a module ship in the bundle.

questions.prompt: Which is the biggest reason to prefer Vite over legacy Webpack configs?

options.text: Faster dev server startup using native ES modules

questions.explanation: Vite serves source over native ESM during dev, giving near-instant startup — bundling happens only for production.

questions.prompt: What is a monorepo?

options.text: Multiple packages stored and versioned in one repository

questions.explanation: Monorepos (Turborepo, Nx, pnpm workspaces) let teams share code, tooling, and CI across multiple packages.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason to use SSR (server-side rendering) or SSG (static generation)?

options.text: Better SEO and first-paint performance for content-heavy pages

questions.explanation: SSR/SSG send ready HTML, improving time-to-content and search engine crawlability compared to client-only SPAs.

questions.prompt: Micro-frontends split a large app into:

options.text: Independently deployable frontend pieces owned by different teams

questions.explanation: Micro-frontends let independent teams ship their own slice of the UI without coordinating a single big release.
